marks.gloss_en: דרבי סבר לה כרבי מאיר ... וסבר לה כרבנן דאמרי שחיטת אמו מטהרתו
the Rabbis: its mother's slaughter purifies it [the ben pekua]

אין, והתנן רבי שמעון אומר: חולין שנשחטו בעזרה ישרפו באש, וכן חיה -- the chaya ruling is explicable only as a decree because of a Torah prohibition (kind svara: no support kind for a בשלמא-argument from a mishna)
R' Shimon holds [the prohibition of] chullin [slaughtered] in the courtyard is Torah law

ותסברא? והאמר רבי מאיר: בן פקועה טעון שחיטה -- for R' Meir even a fetus of a properly slaughtered mother needs its own slaughter, so the case teaches nothing on his view (kind svara: no objection kind for והאמר)
R' Meir: a ben pekua requires slaughter
היכי עביד הכי? והתניא: השוחט וצריך לדם חייב לכסות -- one who slaughters for the blood must still cover it; he should stab or uproot instead
one who slaughters and needs the blood must cover it; how should he act? either stab it or uproot [the simanim]
כי אתא רב דימי אמר: צא טרוף אמר ליה -- Rebbi told him to make it a tereifa first (= p_tze_trof)
כי אתא רבין אמר: צא נחור אמר ליה -- Rebbi told him to stab it (= p_tze_nechor)
Rav Dimi: [Rebbi] said to him: go, make it a tereifa
והתניא רבי אומר: כאשר צויתך -- Rebbi himself derives that a bird's slaughter is from the Torah
(entertained) and if you say [Rebbi] holds there is no Torah slaughter for a bird, and its stabbing is its slaughter
not for everything did R' Meir say an unfit slaughter is called slaughter: R' Meir concedes that it does not permit [the animal] for eating

first answer: [R' Meir's concession] is needed for one who slaughters a tereifa and finds in it a live nine-month fetus -- one might say, since R' Meir holds an unfit slaughter is slaughter, the mother's slaughter serves the fetus and it needs no slaughter of its own

second answer: [the concession] is needed for Rebbi's view -- since the Rabbis say the mother's slaughter purifies it, one might say the [tereifa] mother's slaughter serves [the fetus] and it needs no slaughter; this teaches us otherwise
'and if there die of the animals' (Lev 11:39): some animals defile and some do not -- which? a tereifa that one slaughtered
one who slaughters a tereifa, or slaughters and it is found a tereifa, both chullin in the courtyard -- R' Shimon permits benefit
what the concession teaches: even for R' Shimon, who permits benefit from a tereifa slaughtered as chullin in the courtyard, its slaughter purifies it from nevela impurity
(entertained) but if you say [the prohibition] is rabbinic
moths infested R' Chiyya's flax; he came before Rebbi
